info.title: Adam API
info.description:
Create projects, start and continue AI engineering tasks, run harness tools directly in externally controlled tasks, and retrieve their files.

## External task tools

Create an external task with `POST /v1/tasks/external`; creation performs no inference or compute provisioning. Discover tool schemas with `GET /v1/tasks/{taskId}/tools`, submit calls to `POST /v1/tasks/{taskId}/tool-calls`, and poll `GET /v1/tasks/{taskId}/tool-calls/{callId}` for their durable outcomes. Calls run tools without an Adam agent loop; individual tools may use compute, connected accounts, credentials or billable model services. The explicit `tools:execute` scope grants full harness authority beyond individual read/write scopes. Invocation also requires `tasks:write`. Discovery requires `tasks:read`; result reads require both `tasks:read` and `tools:execute` because outputs can contain workspace and connected-account data. Only external tasks owned by the caller are supported. Reuse the same idempotency key for an identical call. If its outcome is `unknown`, do not automatically retry with a new key: the operation may already have taken effect.

## Authentication

Every endpoint accepts either a personal API key or an Adam ID OAuth 2.0 access token. OAuth clients must request the RFC 8707 resource indicator `https://api.adam.new/v1`; tokens for other Adam resources are rejected.

## Versioning and deprecation

The API is versioned in the URL path (`/v1`). Backwards-compatible additions ship within `/v1`; breaking changes ship as a new major version (`/v2`) alongside the old one. When an endpoint or version is scheduled for removal, its responses carry `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers at least 90 days before the retirement date, and the change is announced at https://adam.new/changelog.

## Rate limits

Every response reports quota via the standard `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers) and the `X-RateLimit-*` set. A `429` includes `Retry-After` in seconds: wait that long before retrying.

## Errors

All 4xx/5xx responses use one JSON shape: `{ "error": { "type", "message", "requestId" } }`, where `type` is a stable machine-readable code (e.g. `invalid_request`, `rate_limit_error`) and `requestId` can be quoted to support.

post.description: Queue a tool call for an external task you own. Use a tool name and input schema from listTaskTools. This runs the selected tool without an Adam agent or model loop; tools may provision compute, use connected accounts or credentials, and incur usage charges. Poll getToolCall for the outcome. An unknown outcome must not be retried with a new key because the operation may have taken effect.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required unique key for this tool call. Reuse it with the same task, tool and input to retrieve the original call rather than execute it again.

get.description: Return a subagent's status, result, and produced file references without starting a parent model turn. Supply exactly one of subagentId or toolCallId; the latter can recover a launch whose tool-call outcome is unknown. Requires tasks:read and tools:execute. Returns null when no matching subagent exists. Internal messages, model routes, and raw errors are omitted.

parameters.name: toolCallId
parameters.description: Launch tool-call identifier. Provide this or subagentId, but not both.

parameters.name: subagentId
parameters.description: Child task UUID. Provide this or toolCallId, but not both.

get.description: Return the durable status, tool output, artifact references, and any execution error for a call in an external task you own. Reading a result never executes the tool again.

personalApiKey.description: A personal API key created in Adam. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

scopes.offline_access: Issue a refresh token so access can be renewed without a new sign-in.
scopes.automations:read: List and inspect automations in the selected workspace.
scopes.automations:write: Create, edit, pause, resume, and delete automations in the selected workspace.
scopes.billing:read: Read subscription, entitlement, and usage information for the selected workspace.
scopes.files:read: List files produced by projects and tasks.
scopes.files:write: Upload task attachments and project files.
scopes.integrations:read: List available and connected integrations in the selected workspace.
scopes.projects:read: List and read projects in the selected workspace.
scopes.projects:write: Create and update projects in the selected workspace.
scopes.tasks:read: List tasks, task status, and task messages.
scopes.tasks:write: Create, update, message, answer, and cancel tasks in the selected workspace.
scopes.tools:execute: Run the full Adam harness in your external tasks, including shell commands, workspace files, connected accounts, paired devices, stored credentials, and billable tools. This grants broad execution authority beyond the individual read and write scopes.

adamId.description: Adam ID OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE (S256). Send resource=https://api.adam.new/v1 on the authorization request and every token request, including refresh-token grants. Protected-resource metadata: https://api.adam.new/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1.

Deprecation.description: RFC 9745 structured-field date (`@<Unix timestamp>`) indicating when this operation became or will become deprecated.

DeprecationLink.description: RFC 8288 Link header with rel="deprecation" pointing to migration guidance. Policy: https://docs.adam.new/api-reference/introduction#versioning-and-deprecation.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594 HTTP-date indicating when a deprecated operation is expected to become unavailable.
